Welcome screen, mode picker, and tutorial
Turn Your Phone into a Smart Keyboard
Turn Your Phone into a Smart Keyboard
Learn more at openterface.com by TechxArtisan
Tap here to open the menu: switch modes, open Welcome & Guide (mode picker and tutorial), or Settings.
Tap the Bluetooth icon to connect via USB or Bluetooth. Green signal bars appear when connected.
Open the menu to choose your preferred input mode: Keyboard & Mouse, Presentation, Shortcuts, Macros, Voice, or Gamepad.
Tap the target OS icon in the header to choose macOS, Windows, or Linux for correct key mappings.
Tap ABC, !?#, or 123 keys on the keyboard to switch between letter, number, and symbol layouts.
The keyboard shortcuts row at the top can be scrolled left or right to reveal more options.
Use the touchpad to control the cursor. Long press to start drag; tap to release.
Failed to open USB device connection
Tap a paired device to connect or disconnect. Long-press to forget.
Disconnect from \"%1$s\"?\nYou can reconnect from this list.
Forget \"%1$s\" (%2$s)?\n\nIt will no longer appear in the paired list.
Bluetooth permission is required to scan and connect. You can grant it in system Settings.
Please select an Openterface or KeyMod device
Only saved devices can be forgotten
Bluetooth not supported on this device
Bluetooth permissions are needed to scan and connect to devices. Please grant them in Settings.
Non-ASCII characters are not supported for HID send. Remove them to enable Send.
Not connected — connect USB or Bluetooth first.
Choose Shortcut Hub profile for this slot
Place a shortcut from your favourites list in this slot.
Add shortcuts to ⭐ Favorites in Shortcut Hub first.
Reset Favorites for \"%1$s\" to the default app list? Your current Favorites order will be lost.
Reset is available only for built-in profiles.
Order — Drag the handle to reorder. Top = first on the keyboard strip; swipe the strip sideways for more pages.
Create — In Favorites, Create adds a new shortcut to General and to Favorites. In General/other tabs, Create adds to that tab only (not Favorites).
Reset — Restores this active built-in profile’s Favorites to fresh-install defaults after confirmation. Custom/imported profiles do not support Reset. Done saves; Cancel discards staged reordering.
No profiles yet.\nTap Create to add one.

Rows 2–3 are shared for every app profile (Default, Blender, …). Use Import / Export here for strip preset JSON: hub button row, strip display mode, favorites order for the active profile, and optional slot overrides.

Choose how much to put in the file:

• Share with anyone — includes full shortcut definitions so someone else can import your row‑1 favorites and strip references even if their app does not already have those shortcuts. Larger file.

• Smaller file — lists shortcut IDs and settings only. Import works when this device (or the recipient) already has the same shortcut IDs in the library. Good for quick backup on your own devices.
Edit rows 2–3 presets, import/export strip JSON, and slot overrides in Shortcut Hub.\n\nCustom slot overrides active: %1$d
This restores the Default shortcut catalog (General tab) and Favorites to a fresh install. Other profiles are not changed.
No favorites yet.\nOpen another tab and use the bookmark to add shortcuts here.
No shortcuts in this profile to add.
No macros yet.\nTap Add to create one.
No valid key events from macro data
Name and sequence appear here as you type.
Sequence — Type text and tokens in Macro sequence. Use Insert tokens for modifiers, keys, and delays. Match opening and closing tags (e.g. <CTRL> … </CTRL>).
Timing — Send char interval sets delay between keystrokes when the macro runs.
Scheduler — Optional: pick a run time and repeat options. Tap Save when finished.
Where it saves — The shortcut is added to General in Shortcut Hub and to your Favorites strip. To change the name, icon, or order, open Shortcut Hub.

Keys — Toggle modifiers, then tap one letter or key chip. Chips wrap to more lines on small screens. Advanced lets you type token syntax (e.g. <CTRL>c</CTRL>) instead; choosing a chip clears Advanced.

Modifiers & Target OS — Button labels match your current Target OS (header in the main app). The first toggle is ⌘ / Win / Super (HID Gui), then Ctrl, Shift, and Opt / Alt. Stored shortcuts use the same bits as the keyboard; when you change Target OS, labels and HID mapping update together.
Pick a key below, or use Advanced.
No Shortcut Hub profile is active.
Choose a key or enter advanced shortcut data.
No valid key found in shortcut data.
This shortcut already exists in this profile.
Use the tabs above to browse shortcuts, tap the bookmark icon to add to Favorites, then return here to drag and reorder.
Drag components to reposition, tap Done when finished.
Shortcut strip: showing shortcut names. Tap to switch to icons.
Shortcut strip: showing icons. Tap to switch to combo text.
Shortcut strip: showing combo keys (e.g. Alt+X). Tap to switch to names.
Type and edit long text here — tap Send to send it to the connected device
Tip: Long-press this key to lock the modifier.
Connect USB or Bluetooth to send keystrokes.
Send types the buffered text on the host. In Compose mode, keystrokes are not sent until you tap Send.
Switch to direct HID: each key sends as you type
Switch to compose: type a buffer, then tap Send
Keys send out directly as you type
Ready — set API key in Settings
